items.title: 52220_Woody Herman oral history interview
items.q: And we had another young man in the saxophone section, along with myself. His name was Tony Martin.

ctx.x: Tom Garen was a very important influence on me, because I think he taught me a very great deal about music as a business. Tom was a businessman, and he was not in any sense of the word a musician you would look up to as an incentive to want to play better or something. But he did have a good sense of logic and he had a feeling for what the public would like. And the truth of the matter is that I would say that the majority of the bands during the late -- early '30s, actually, and even later, were really built on…

It was entirely up to the person's own judgment as to whether -- how important music was going to be in his particular band. And I learned a great deal from Tom, not because it was the best musical band I worked in, but because it was a great entertainment band. He had some very important people in the band, like Ginny Simms, a girl singer who later went to Kay Kyser's band. And we had another young man in the saxophone section, along with myself. His name was Tony Martin. It was then Al Morris, and later in the…
